title: Microsoft confirms November hotpatch can stop some apps installing or starting on Windows 11
summary: Microsoft told IT administrators in service alert WI1559710, reported by BleepingComputer, that devices with the November 2026 hotpatch, delivered through Windows Autopatch to Windows 11 24H2 and later, may show error 0xC0000099 when installing, launching or running some apps, mainly those loading the 32-bit msi.dll. Standard November Patch Tuesday updates are not affected. Microsoft gives a registry workaround until a fix is available; heise advises against uninstalling the hotpatch.
plain: Microsoft says a November hotpatch can stop some apps from installing or starting on Windows 11 machines updated through Autopatch. A registry workaround is available.
exec: Microsoft confirms hotpatched Windows 11 fleets may see some apps fail to install or start.
action: Microsoft's workaround, as reported by BleepingComputer: back up the registry, set HotPatchTableSize under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Memory Management to 2000 (heise gives the value as hexadecimal), then restart. heise advises not uninstalling the hotpatch.
